title: Choosing the Right Site
summary: Compare hypothetical sites by considering infrastructure, risk, access, and community context.
objectives: Compare site choices using more than one constraint.
Explain why a site with one strength may still have important tradeoffs.

vocab.def: Choosing a location after considering needs, limits, and risks.
The ability to reach a place or connect it to needed services.
A possibility that could cause harm, delay, or loss.

sections.heading: A location affects the whole system
sections.body: A site may need access to electricity, fiber, roads, workers, and emergency services. Land, weather, flooding, nearby communities, and environmental conditions can also matter.

sections.heading: Compare three hypothetical sites
sections.body: Site A has strong power but poor fiber. Site B has strong fiber but limited land. Site C has more land but is farther from supporting infrastructure. No site wins every category.

sections.heading: Explain the tradeoff
sections.body: Rank the sites using criteria your team names. A defensible choice explains what it gains, what it gives up, and what additional evidence is needed.

practice.prompt: Choose one hypothetical site and list two strengths, one concern, and one question you would investigate before deciding.

quiz.question: Why should a design team consider fiber access when choosing a site?
options: Connectivity supports the usefulness and reliability of the facility
Fiber makes land and weather irrelevant
Fiber removes the need for people
quiz.answer: Connectivity supports the usefulness and reliability of the facility

reflectionPrompt: Which site-selection factor would you want more evidence about before making a decision?
